alt.en: A standing wooden Mangaaka figure with hands on its hips and iron blades and nails inserted into its torso.
alt.zh: 站立的木雕曼加阿卡像，双手叉腰，躯干插有铁片和铁钉。

caption.en: Yombe-Kongo artist and nganga, about 1880–1900, Chiloango River region, Republic of the Congo or Cabinda, Angola. The Metropolitan Museum of Art, 2008.30. Carving and ritual additions contributed to the figure’s work in oath-taking and dispute resolution.
caption.zh: 约1880—1900年，约姆贝—刚果雕刻者与恩甘加仪式专家共同制作，来自刚果共和国或安哥拉卡宾达的希洛安戈河地区。大都会艺术博物馆藏，2008.30。雕刻与仪式中添加的材料共同参与了起誓和处理争端的实践。

interpretation.en: A modern museum photograph of a historical ritual object. The figure is not a portrait of a named maker or ruler; the catalogue attributes it to artistic and ritual collaboration.
interpretation.zh: 这是一件历史仪式物品的现代博物馆照片，并非某位具名工匠或统治者的肖像；馆方将其归于雕刻与仪式实践的合作。

alt.zh: 长条锈蚀铁刃、细长剑柄及装饰配件。

interpretation.en: A period object, not a weapon attributed to a named king, makes early Frankish military equipment tangible.
interpretation.zh: 这是时代实物，并非归属于某位国王的武器，使早期法兰克军事装备具体可见。

caption.zh: 这件约800至825年的象牙牌以圣母象征教会。

alt.en: An ivory relief of a seated, haloed woman beneath an ornate arch.
alt.zh: 象牙浮雕：带光环的女子坐在装饰拱门下。

interpretation.en: A surviving Carolingian carving shows how Christian institutions were expressed through figures and precious materials.
interpretation.zh: 存世加洛林雕刻展示基督教机构如何通过人物及贵重材料获得视觉表达。

caption.en: A setting of about 950–1000 surrounds an imperial sapphire intaglio dated 337–350. The Met tentatively locates the setting in the Rhineland.
caption.zh: 约950至1000年的镶座环绕337至350年的帝王蓝宝石凹雕；大都会暂将镶座产地定为莱茵地区。

alt.en: A blue profile intaglio surrounded by a circular gold brooch and pale pearls.
alt.zh: 蓝色侧面头像凹雕，外有圆形金胸针及浅色珍珠。

interpretation.en: The dates distinguish an ancient image from its medieval reuse. This is material evidence of reworking, not an unbroken political succession.
interpretation.zh: 年代区分古代图像与中世纪再利用，体现材料改造，而非未中断的政治继承。

caption.en: Carved ornament and Latin lettering commemorate Justinian’s consulship in 521, before he became emperor in 527.
caption.zh: 雕刻装饰与拉丁铭文纪念查士丁尼于521年担任执政官，早于他527年即帝位。

alt.en: A tall ivory panel with an inscribed central medallion and symmetrical ornament.
alt.zh: 高长象牙板，中央为带铭文的圆章，周围饰纹对称分布。

interpretation.en: This consular diptych panel connects Eastern Roman court culture with an older Roman office; it is not a page from Justinian’s law compilation.
interpretation.zh: 执政官双联板将东罗马宫廷文化与更古老的罗马官职联系起来，并非《查士丁尼法典》书页。

alt.zh: 浅色星形砖面布满金褐色枝叶纹与边缘文字。

caption.zh: 在萨姆纳堡签署的条约使迪内人得以离开拘禁并返回部分家园。

alt.en: Commissioners’ signatures and named Navajo signatories’ marks on a treaty page.

items.creator: Cherokee petitioners of Aquohee and Taquoee districts

caption.en: Petitioners asked the United States Senate not to ratify an agreement made without authorization from their national council or people.
caption.zh: 请愿者请求美国参议院不要批准未经其民族议会或民众授权订立的协议。

alt.en: A handwritten petition protesting the New Echota treaty.
alt.zh: 反对新埃乔塔条约的手写请愿书。

caption.en: Hatshepsut appears in a royal seated statue from her reign, around 1473–1458 BCE.
caption.zh: 哈特谢普苏特以王室坐像呈现，制作于其在位时期，约公元前1473至1458年。

alt.en: A pale stone seated royal figure with hands resting on the knees.
alt.zh: 浅色石雕王者端坐，双手置于膝上。

interpretation.en: A surviving royal image makes New Kingdom kingship visible. It is an ancient representation of Hatshepsut, not a modern reconstruction of her appearance.
interpretation.zh: 存世王室形象使新王国王权具体可见；这是哈特谢普苏特的古代形象，并非现代容貌重建。

title.zh: 梅克特雷的面包房与酿酒坊模型

caption.en: This funerary model from the tomb of the royal chief steward Meketre represents bread and beer production.
caption.zh: 来自王室总管梅克特雷墓的随葬模型，表现面包与啤酒的生产。

alt.en: Small painted workers and equipment arranged within a model building.
alt.zh: 模型建筑内排列彩绘工人与设备。

interpretation.en: The model links an official’s burial provision to organized labor. It represents idealized work for the afterlife, not an excavated working bakery.
interpretation.zh: 模型将官员的墓葬供养与有组织劳动联系起来；它表现理想化的来世劳作，并非发掘出的实际面包房。

caption.en: A Median figure once formed part of a palace stairway relief at Persepolis, dated around 405–359 BCE.
caption.zh: 约公元前405至359年的米底人物，原属波斯波利斯宫殿阶梯浮雕。

alt.en: A carved limestone figure in a rounded cap and belted tunic, with a hand extending toward another figure.
alt.zh: 石灰岩浮雕人物戴圆帽、着束腰衣，手伸向另一人物。

interpretation.en: The fragment belongs to the western stairway of Darius’s palace and makes imperial ceremony tangible. Its date is later than the palace founder’s reign.
interpretation.zh: 残片来自大流士宫西侧阶梯，使帝国礼仪具体可见；其制作年代晚于宫殿创建者在位时期。

title.en: Bahram Gur’s Skill with the Bow

caption.en: This illustrated folio was made around 1430 in Baysunghur’s Herat workshop; the manuscript’s calligrapher was Maulana Azhar.
caption.zh: 这张插图书叶约1430年制作于拜宋豁尔的赫拉特作坊，手稿书法家为毛拉纳·阿兹哈尔。

alt.en: A painted hunting scene with riders and animals beneath a panel of manuscript text.
alt.zh: 手稿文字栏下方绘有骑者与动物的狩猎场景。

interpretation.en: The folio is direct evidence of Timurid book production. Its literary scene is not a report of a fifteenth-century hunt, and Nizami’s text predates this copy.
interpretation.zh: 书叶直接反映帖木儿时代制书；文学场景并非十五世纪狩猎实录，尼扎米原作也早于此抄本。

caption.en: This glass lamp of about 1329–1335 names the Mamluk patron Qawsun and was probably intended for one of his Cairo foundations.
caption.zh: 约1329至1335年的玻璃灯铭记马穆鲁克赞助者考孙，可能原拟用于其开罗宗教设施之一。

alt.en: A wide-necked glass lamp with colored enamel inscriptions, gilding and suspension loops.
alt.zh: 广口玻璃灯饰彩色珐琅铭文、金彩及悬挂环。

interpretation.en: A named commission connects elite patronage with public religious buildings. Its precise original building and attribution to the maker remain qualified.
interpretation.zh: 有明确赞助者的委托将精英赞助与公共宗教建筑联系起来；具体原属建筑与制作者归属仍保留疑问。

title.en: Benin plaque: Portuguese traders and manillas
title.zh: 贝宁浮雕：葡萄牙商人与马尼拉铜环

caption.en: Edo brass-casting guild artists made this palace plaque around 1540–1570. Portuguese figures appear with manillas, linking trade and material wealth.
caption.zh: 埃多铸铜行会艺术家约于1540至1570年制作此宫殿浮雕；葡萄牙人物与马尼拉铜环并置，将贸易与物质财富联系起来。

alt.en: A tall brass plaque with human figures and curved manilla forms in relief.
alt.zh: 高长黄铜浮雕板，上有人物与弧形马尼拉铜环。

interpretation.en: A court-made image gives a Benin perspective on overseas exchange. The material is brass, and the plaque predates the British attack of 1897; it is not a picture of that attack.
interpretation.zh: 宫廷制作的图像呈现贝宁对海外交换的视角。材质是黄铜，制作早于1897年英国进攻，并非该次进攻的图像。

caption.en: A ceramic portrait vessel dated 500–800 CE joins a modeled face to the stirrup-spout bottle form used on Peru’s northern coast.
caption.zh: 这件公元500至800年的陶制肖像器，将塑造的人脸与秘鲁北海岸使用的马镫形口瓶结合。

alt.en: A ceramic bottle shaped as a human head, with painted headwear and a tall spout visible behind it.
alt.zh: 人头形陶瓶戴彩绘头饰，后方可见高直瓶口。

interpretation.en: The vessel makes the entry’s account of skilled workshops and elite imagery tangible. Its individuality does not identify a named ruler or prove a single centralized Moche empire.
interpretation.zh: 器皿使本条所述工坊技艺与精英形象具体可见；独特面貌不能确定具名统治者，也不能证明单一中央集权莫切帝国。

title.en: Olmec mask in serpentinite and albitite
title.zh: 蛇纹岩与钠长岩制奥尔梅克面具

caption.en: This small mask, dated 1000–400 BCE, combines serpentinite and albitite. It offers a close view of the stone-working traditions discussed in the entry.
caption.zh: 这件公元前1000至400年的小型面具采用蛇纹岩与钠长岩，可近观本条讨论的石工传统。

alt.en: A small smooth greenish stone face with narrow eyes and parted lips.
alt.zh: 小型光滑绿色石雕面孔，眼睛细长，嘴唇微张。

interpretation.en: The museum identifies the materials precisely; “greenstone” need not mean jade. No particular ruler, ritual use or excavation at San Lorenzo is established for this object here.
interpretation.zh: 馆方明确鉴定材质，“绿石”并不必然是玉。此处不认定具体统治者、仪式用途，或断言本件出土于圣洛伦索。

title.en: Shiva Nataraja: a Chola-period copper-alloy image
title.zh: 湿婆舞王：朱罗时代铜合金造像

caption.en: This Tamil Nadu sculpture dates to the late twelfth or early thirteenth century. Images of this type were carried in festival processions.
caption.zh: 这件泰米尔纳德邦雕像制作于十二世纪末至十三世纪初；同类造像用于节庆巡游。

alt.en: Shiva dances with multiple arms inside a flaming ring, one foot raised.
alt.zh: 湿婆在火焰圆环内起舞，多臂展开，一足抬起。

interpretation.en: Portable sacred sculpture complements the entry’s monumental temples: casting skills also produced images that moved through public space. No commission by a specific Chola ruler is claimed.
interpretation.zh: 可移动神像补充了本条的宏大寺院：铸造技艺也制作穿行公共空间的形象。不声称本件由某位朱罗君王委托。

caption.en: The Met dates this gray-schist Maitreya to about the third century. Small donors on its base venerate a reliquary beneath a canopy.
caption.zh: 大都会将这尊灰色片岩弥勒像定为约三世纪；基座的小型供养人礼敬华盖下的舍利容器。

alt.en: A standing robed bodhisattva with a topknot above a base carved with smaller figures.
alt.zh: 站立披衣菩萨头饰发髻，基座雕有较小人物。

interpretation.en: The entry describes Buddhist workshops within Kushan-era networks. This Gandharan devotional object shows sacred imagery and donors, without implying that a Kushan king commissioned it or that all regional art followed one model.
interpretation.zh: 本条讨论贵霜时代网络中的佛教工坊。犍陀罗供奉造像呈现神圣形象与供养人，不暗示贵霜君王委托，也不认为区域艺术皆遵循同一模式。

interpretation.zh: 飘扬的衣袍把归隐表现为富有动势的行旅。作品距陶渊明在世逾千年，属于其文学接受史。

items.creator: Zhao Mengfu (1254–1322), per Palace Museum catalogue
items.date: Yuan dynasty; later inscriptions and mounting

interpretation.en: The comparatively small figure is enveloped by writing and seals. The scroll records Du Fu’s reception centuries after his life, rather than witnessing a Tang event.
interpretation.zh: 相对小幅的人像被文字与印章环绕。画卷记录杜甫身后数百年的接受史，而不是唐代事件的现场见证。

title.en: Wang Mang in an illustrated Han narrative
title.zh: 汉代通俗叙事中的王莽像

alt.en: A seated bearded figure in a winged official hat appears below a hostile verse identifying Wang Mang.
alt.zh: 戴展脚官帽的蓄须坐像上方，题诗点名王莽并作贬斥。

caption.en: Later depiction: Wang Mang in an illustrated Han narrative. Undated historical woodblock edition.
caption.zh: 后世图像：汉代通俗叙事中的王莽像，历史木刻刊本，出版年代未详。

interpretation.en: The verse condemns Wang Mang before the reader reaches the story. Image and text make visible the hostile reputation inherited by later popular histories of the Han.
interpretation.zh: 读者尚未进入故事，题诗已对王莽作出谴责；图文共同呈现后世汉代通俗史书所继承的敌意评价。

title.en: Yu Qian, painted by Gu Jianlong

alt.en: An official in a red robe and tall red-and-black crown faces forward, holding an ivory-colored tablet.
alt.zh: 官员穿红袍，戴红黑相间的高冠，面朝前方，手持象牙色笏板。

caption.en: Later depiction: Yu Qian, painted by Gu Jianlong. 17th century.
caption.zh: 后世图像：顾见龙绘于谦像，17世纪。

interpretation.en: The tablet, frontal pose and ceremonial clothing commemorate service to the state. Gu Jianlong painted Yu Qian roughly two centuries after the minister’s execution.
interpretation.zh: 笏板、正面姿态与礼服纪念于谦的国家臣僚身份；顾见龙作画时，距离这位大臣被处死已约两百年。

title.en: Zhang Qian’s mission in a Dunhuang mural
title.zh: 敦煌壁画中的张骞出使

alt.en: A damaged mural shows an imperial figure with attendants at left and a mounted envoy beneath a canopy at right.
alt.zh: 残损壁画左侧是帝王与侍从，右侧是华盖下骑马的使者。

caption.en: Later depiction: Zhang Qian’s mission in a Dunhuang mural. High Tang, approximately 8th century.
caption.zh: 后世图像：敦煌壁画中的张骞出使，盛唐，约8世纪。

interpretation.en: Tang-period Dunhuang painters placed Zhang Qian’s Han mission within a religious history of connections to the west. The scene records a later interpretation of travel and diplomacy.
interpretation.zh: 唐代敦煌画师把张骞的汉代出使置入与西方联系的宗教历史中；画面留下的是后世对旅行与外交的解释。

alt.en: Columns of black Chinese writing and smaller annotations run across aged paper; red seals appear near the end of the text.

caption.zh: 后世图像：明代张良立像，明代（1368—1644）。

interpretation.en: The restrained pose commemorates Zhang Liang as an adviser rather than a battlefield commander. This Ming portrait belongs to the later visual tradition surrounding the founding of Han.
interpretation.zh: 克制的姿态将张良纪念为谋臣，而非阵前统帅；这幅明代画像属于围绕汉朝开国形成的后世视觉传统。

title.en: A Jingdezhen kendi for connected markets
title.zh: 面向跨域市场的景德镇军持

alt.en: A white porcelain pouring vessel has a tall neck and rounded side spout, painted in cobalt blue with fruits and flowers.
alt.zh: 白瓷注器有高颈与圆鼓侧流，器身以钴蓝描绘花果。

caption.en: A Jingdezhen kendi for connected markets. Late 16th century; museum photograph undated.
caption.zh: 面向跨域市场的景德镇军持，16世纪晚期；馆藏照片拍摄年代未标明。

interpretation.en: The neck and side spout distinguish a kendi from a European-style handled jug. Blue flowers and fruit spread across a form made at Jingdezhen for uses within connected Asian markets.
interpretation.zh: 高颈与侧流使军持有别于带把的欧式水壶；景德镇在这种面向亚洲跨域市场的器形上绘出青花花果。

alt.en: A crowded arched wooden bridge spans a river filled with boats; porters, pack animals, stalls and tiled roofs line the banks.
alt.zh: 拥挤的拱形木桥横跨有船往来的河流，两岸可见脚夫、驮兽、摊位与瓦屋。

caption.en: River traffic and bridge crowds in the Qingming scroll. Northern Song dynasty (960–1127).
caption.zh: 《清明上河图》中的船运与桥市，北宋（960—1127）。

interpretation.en: Follow the boat crews, people crossing the bridge and goods arriving along the bank. The scene joins transport and trade to the work that kept a Song city supplied.
interpretation.zh: 沿画面追踪船工、过桥行人与沿岸运抵的货物，可以看到运输、交易和维持宋代城市供给的劳动如何相连。

title.zh: 先贤像册中的郭子仪（右）

alt.en: An open album shows two men in dark caps with inscriptions above; Guo Ziyi is the right-hand portrait, identified as leaf 35.
alt.zh: 展开的像册绘两位戴深色帽的男子，上方各有题字；右页第35幅为郭子仪。

caption.en: Later depiction: Guo Ziyi in an album of worthies, at right. Historical album; exact date unestablished.
caption.zh: 后世图像：先贤像册中的郭子仪（右），历史像册，确切年代未定。

interpretation.en: The inscription praises Guo Ziyi’s military service and descendants. This later album preserves a model of the loyal minister; its facing portraits also reveal how exemplary lives were collected together.

title.en: Han Xin and Xiao He in an album of ministers
title.zh: 贤臣像册中的韩信与萧何

alt.en: Two full-length line portraits face each other across an album opening; the left label names Han Xin and the right names Xiao He.
alt.zh: 两幅全身白描像在册页对开中相向而立；左页题韩信，右页题萧何。

alt.zh: 张仲景留须、手持展开的书，站在木刻边框内，上方题“医圣张仲景”。

caption.en: Woodcut from Bencao mengquan, an edition engraved during the Wanli reign, 1573–1620. Wellcome Collection, L0039319. The design tradition is attributed to Gan Bozong of the Tang period; the surviving print is Ming.
caption.zh: 《本草蒙筌》万历年间（1573—1620）刊本木刻像。Wellcome Collection藏，L0039319。图像传统归于唐代甘伯宗，现存印本则是明代。

items.creator: Anonymous Ming woodcut maker; image tradition attributed to Gan Bozong

interpretation.en: This later medical book commemorates Zhang Zhongjing and the transmission of his writings. It is neither a Han-period portrait nor a surviving page of his original treatise.
interpretation.zh: 这部后世医书纪念张仲景及其著作的传承；它既不是汉代肖像，也不是《伤寒杂病论》原稿的遗页。

title.en: Taizong in a Ming standing portrait

alt.en: Taizong stands in a yellow robe with colored dragons, a black cap and black shoes, holding a decorated belt with both hands.
alt.zh: 唐太宗戴黑帽、穿饰彩龙的黄袍与黑鞋，双手握住装饰腰带站立。

caption.en: Standing Portrait of Emperor Tang Taizong (I), anonymous, Ming dynasty. National Palace Museum, Taipei, 中畫000263. The museum records a remounting in 1748, centuries after the Tang ruler’s life.

items.institution: National Palace Museum, Taipei, 中畫000263

interpretation.zh: 龙袍与正式姿态呈现后世王朝塑造的帝王形象。1748年题记标明重装时间，不是原画创作年代，也不是太宗在位年代。

alt.en: Sun Quan stands in a black and red robe with a ceremonial crown, holding a feather fan between two attendants; the upper-left inscription names him.
alt.zh: 孙权戴垂旒冠、穿黑红礼服，持羽扇立于两名侍从之间，左上题字标明“吴主孙权”。

caption.en: Detail of The Thirteen Emperors, traditionally attributed to Yan Liben. Museum of Fine Arts, Boston, Denman Waldo Ross Collection, 31.643. The seventh-century scroll includes later replacement sections; Sun Quan belongs to its early group of rulers.

title.en: Sima Yi in a Ming book of historical portraits
title.zh: 明代古人像册中的司马懿

alt.en: Black-and-white half-length portrait of a bearded Sima Yi in a folded cap, hands inside his sleeves, with his name at upper right and verse at upper left.
alt.zh: 司马懿戴折巾、留须、双手笼袖的黑白半身像，右上题姓名，左上有赞辞。

caption.en: Sima Yi in Lidai guren xiangzan, a portrait book published in Hongzhi 11 (1498). Zhu Tianran wrote the encomia; the illustrator is unnamed. Digital reproduction via Wikimedia Commons.
caption.zh: 《历代古人像赞》中的司马懿像，该书刊于弘治十一年（1498）。朱天然撰赞，绘者无名。数字复制图由维基共享资源提供。

items.date: Book published 1498; precise impression date not established
items.institution: Lidai guren xiangzan; reproduction via Wikimedia Commons

interpretation.en: The adjacent verse recognizes military talent while condemning ambition and concentrated power. That judgment belongs to a Ming portrait book, centuries after Sima Yi’s life.
interpretation.zh: 旁侧赞辞肯定统兵才干，却批评野心与专权。这一评价来自明代像册，距离司马懿在世已逾千年。

title.en: Yue Fei in a Ming seated portrait

alt.en: Yue Fei sits in a brown robe with colorful dragon-like motifs, a blue cloth cap and black boots, holding an open blue-covered book above a red belt with pale jade plaques.
alt.zh: 岳飞戴蓝巾、穿饰彩色蟒纹的褐袍与黑靴端坐，双手捧蓝皮书，腰系嵌浅色玉牌的红带。

caption.en: Anonymous Ming portrait of Yue Fei, ink and color on silk, Palace Museum, Beijing. The museum identifies his embroidered python robe, jade belt and book, explaining that the dress follows Ming conventions.
caption.zh: 明代无款《岳飞像》轴，绢本设色，北京故宫博物院藏。馆方说明画中织金蟒袍、玉带与书册，并指出衣冠依照明代制度绘制。

items.creator: Anonymous Ming painter

interpretation.en: The painting belongs to Yue Fei’s later commemoration. Its Ming-style official dress is evidence of the painter’s historical setting, not a record of Southern Song military uniform.
interpretation.zh: 画作属于对岳飞的后世纪念。明式官服反映画家所处的历史环境，并非南宋军装的记录。

title.en: Kongo crucifix: Christianity in an African court
title.zh: 刚果十字架：非洲宫廷中的基督教

alt.en: A metal figure of Christ fixed to a tall wooden cross, with a smaller figure below.
alt.zh: 金属基督像固定在高木十字架上，下方另有一尊较小人物像。

caption.en: Kongo artist, 16th–17th century, with later additions. Cast metals and wood turn the Christian cross into an object made and used within Kongo religious life.
caption.zh: 刚果艺术家制作，16至17世纪，含后期增添部分。铸造金属与木材使基督教十字架成为刚果宗教生活中制作和使用的实物。

interpretation.en: The crucifix makes the entries’ account of local adaptation tangible: conversion created new diplomatic and devotional connections without ending Kongo political agency. Its surviving form developed after the royal conversion of 1491.
interpretation.zh: 这件十字架使两篇条目所述的本土转化具体可见：改宗带来外交与信仰联系，刚果仍是主动的政治参与者。现存形态形成于1491年王室改宗之后。

alt.en: A seated woman rests her cheek on her right hand amid sculpted terracotta foliage and rocks.
alt.zh: 一位坐着的女子以右手托腮，四周为陶塑植物和岩石。

caption.en: Java, 14th–15th century. This terracotta surround once decorated a column of a pavilion-like building in the Majapahit artistic tradition.
caption.zh: 爪哇，14至15世纪。这件陶制柱饰属于满者伯夷艺术传统，原用于装饰亭阁式建筑的柱子。

interpretation.en: The entry’s urban landscape included houses and skilled clay workers as well as royal monuments. The museum connects such column ornaments with the capital near Trowulan; the woman may have belonged to a larger narrative scene.
interpretation.zh: 条目中的城市景观不仅有王室纪念建筑，也有住宅和熟练陶工。博物馆将此类柱饰同特罗武兰附近的都城联系起来；女子可能原属一组叙事场景。

title.en: Shah Tahmasp’s Book of Kings: a ruler dictates reforms
title.zh: 塔赫马斯普《列王纪》：君王口授改革

alt.en: A richly bordered manuscript page shows a seated ruler addressing a scribe and courtiers beneath columns of Persian verse.
alt.zh: 装饰华丽的手稿页中，君王坐着向书记和廷臣讲话，上方排列波斯诗文。

caption.en: Painting attributed to Muzaffar Ali, about 1530–1535, for Shah Tahmasp’s Shahnama. The literary scene portrays Nushirvan, the sixth-century Sasanian king, announcing reforms.
caption.zh: 绘画归于穆扎法尔·阿里，约1530至1535年，出自塔赫马斯普《列王纪》。文学场景描绘六世纪萨珊君王努希尔万宣布改革。

interpretation.en: The folio is evidence of Safavid workshop patronage and ideas of just kingship. Its sixteenth-century production date is distinct from the sixth-century reign it imagines; Firdausi wrote the poem, not this painting.
interpretation.zh: 此页展示萨法维宫廷作坊的资助与公正王权观念。十六世纪的制作时间须与画中想象的六世纪统治时期区分；菲尔多西是诗歌作者，并非此画画家。

title.en: Süleiman’s tughra: government in gold and blue
title.zh: 苏莱曼图格拉：金蓝交织的行政权威

alt.en: An Ottoman calligraphic insignia forms long blue-and-gold loops, three tall strokes and a horizontal extension on pale paper.
alt.zh: 浅色纸上的奥斯曼花押由金蓝长环、三道高竖笔和横向延伸笔画组成。

caption.en: Istanbul, about 1555–1560. Süleiman’s tughra combines the ruler’s name and titles with an elaborate gold-and-blue floral design.
caption.zh: 伊斯坦布尔，约1555至1560年。苏莱曼的图格拉将君主名号与精细的金蓝花卉纹样结合。

interpretation.en: Royal edicts carried this form of sovereign authentication. The design connects imperial administration with specialist calligraphy and illumination, showing how workshop skills served government.
interpretation.zh: 王令使用这种形式认证君权。图案把帝国行政与专业书法、描金装饰相连，展示作坊技艺如何服务政府。

title.en: Akbar hunting: imperial prowess in a court manuscript
title.zh: 阿克巴狩猎：宫廷手稿中的帝王勇武

alt.en: A mounted emperor lunges toward a lioness while another horseman shoots backward amid rocks and trees.
alt.zh: 骑马的皇帝俯身刺向母狮，另一骑者在山石树木之间回身放箭。

caption.en: Late-sixteenth-century folio from an Akbarnama, probably made in Lahore. The painting presents Akbar’s hunt as a display of courage and royal command.
caption.zh: 十六世纪晚期《阿克巴纪》书页，可能制作于拉合尔。绘画将阿克巴狩猎表现为勇气与帝王统御的展示。

interpretation.en: The Mughal overview and Akbar biography both discuss collaborative imperial bookmaking. This courtly representation makes that work visible while revealing how a chronicle fashioned its ruler’s public image.
interpretation.zh: 莫卧儿概述和阿克巴传记都讨论宫廷书籍的协作生产。此图使这种劳动可见，也展示编年史如何塑造君主形象。

title.en: Glass mosaic pieces from Abbasid Samarra
title.zh: 阿拔斯萨迈拉的玻璃马赛克块

alt.en: Twelve small glass mosaic pieces in muted green, blue and dark tones are arranged in a grid.
alt.zh: 十二枚绿、蓝及深色的小玻璃马赛克块排列成网格。

caption.en: Samarra, Iraq, ninth century. These glass tesserae survive from the decorative materials of the Abbasid capital.
caption.zh: 伊拉克萨迈拉，九世纪。这些玻璃马赛克块保存了阿拔斯都城使用的装饰材料。

interpretation.en: Small reflective fragments reveal the material choices behind monumental palace interiors. The museum reports relatively few glass tesserae from Samarra, where glass remained a valued expression of imperial taste.
interpretation.zh: 细小的反光碎块展示宏大宫殿内部的材料选择。博物馆指出萨迈拉出土的玻璃马赛克较少，玻璃仍是受重视的宫廷审美表现。

title.en: Maya column: royal costume and public display
title.zh: 玛雅石柱：王室服饰与公开展示

alt.en: A carved limestone column depicts an elaborately dressed figure with a towering headdress and a smaller attendant to the side.
alt.zh: 石灰岩柱雕刻一位衣饰繁复、头戴高冠的人物，侧面有一位较小的侍从。

caption.en: Maya artists, Mexico, 800–900 CE. A likely ruler carries a blade and shield beneath a layered headdress; traces of pigment remain.
caption.zh: 玛雅艺术家，墨西哥，公元800至900年。可能为统治者的人物戴层叠头冠，持刃与盾；表面尚存颜料痕迹。

interpretation.en: The Puuc-region carving links authority to warfare, ritual and ancestry through costume. Its unnamed subject illustrates royal self-presentation across Maya courts without assigning this unprovenanced monument to Tikal or a single Maya empire.
interpretation.zh: 这件普克地区风格雕刻通过服饰，将权威同战争、仪式和祖先相连。人物姓名未明，展示玛雅宫廷的王权表达；不把缺乏确切出土地的石柱归给蒂卡尔或单一玛雅帝国。

title.zh: 印加统治下的丘基班巴束腰衫

alt.en: A rectangular woven tunic is covered with a dense red, yellow and dark grid of eight-pointed stars and small geometric motifs.
alt.zh: 长方形织物束腰衫布满红、黄及深色网格，其中排列八角星和小型几何图案。

caption.en: Chuquibamba artist, Peru, 1460–1540; camelid hair and cotton. Local star patterns coexist with proportions associated with Inca tunics.
caption.zh: 丘基班巴织工，秘鲁，1460至1540年；驼科动物毛与棉。本地星纹与印加束腰衫的比例特征并存。

interpretation.en: The entry describes local traditions continuing within imperial administration. The museum now attributes this tunic to Chuquibamba makers rather than treating every imperial-period textile as an Inca court product.
interpretation.zh: 条目强调本地传统在帝国行政下延续。博物馆现将此衣归于丘基班巴织工，而非把帝国时期所有织物都当作印加宫廷产品。

title.en: Asante gold lion: royal authority in a portable ornament
title.zh: 阿散蒂金狮：饰物中的王权

alt.en: A hollow gold lion stands on an oval base, its head turned sideways, mouth open and tail curled over its back.
alt.zh: 中空金狮站在椭圆底座上，侧转头部、张嘴，尾巴卷向背部。

caption.en: Asante-Akan artist, Kumasi, Ghana, nineteenth century. Gold and heraldic animal imagery express the authority and qualities of a ruler.
caption.zh: 阿散蒂—阿坎艺术家，加纳库马西，十九世纪。黄金与纹章式动物形象表达统治者的权威和品质。

interpretation.en: The object connects the entry’s gold economy and courtly symbols. Asante artists adapted the lion into a language of chiefly strength and wisdom; the precise original mounting of this ornament is uncertain.
interpretation.zh: 这件饰物将条目中的黄金经济和宫廷象征相连。阿散蒂艺术家把狮子转化为首领力量与智慧的表达；其原有安装位置尚不确定。

title.en: A Buddha head from late Gupta Mathura

alt.en: A reddish stone Buddha head has downcast eyes, softly modeled cheeks and rows of small curls.
alt.zh: 红色石质佛首双目下垂、面颊柔和，头部排列细小卷发。

caption.en: Mathura, northern India, late fifth–early sixth century. The head belonged to a nearly life-size Buddha figure in the late Gupta artistic tradition.
caption.zh: 北印度秣菟罗，五世纪晚期至六世纪初。此佛首原属接近真人大小的佛像，体现笈多晚期艺术传统。

interpretation.en: Idealized features and carefully joined curved planes communicate meditative inwardness. The sculpture gives a concrete form to the entry’s account of devotional art and the development of classical styles.
interpretation.zh: 理想化五官与衔接细腻的曲面表现内省禅思。雕塑使条目中关于宗教艺术及古典风格发展的叙述具体可见。

title.en: Standing and fallen stelae at Aksum
title.zh: 阿克苏姆直立与倒卧的石碑

alt.en: Tall stone stelae stand beside a much larger broken monument lying on the ground.
alt.zh: 高耸石碑旁，一座更大的残断石碑横卧地面。

caption.en: The stelae field at Aksum, photographed in 2012. Monumental stone building expressed elite and royal authority.
caption.zh: 2012年拍摄的阿克苏姆石碑区。巨型石构工程表达精英与王室权威。

interpretation.en: Compare the scale of standing and fallen stones to consider quarrying, transport and collective labour.
interpretation.zh: 比较直立与倒卧石材的尺度，思考开采、运输和集体劳动。

caption.en: Excavated structures at Caral in Peru’s Supe Valley, photographed in 2022. The canopy belongs to modern conservation, not the ancient settlement.
caption.zh: 2022年拍摄的秘鲁苏佩河谷卡拉尔建筑遗迹。棚顶属于现代保护设施，而非古代聚落。

interpretation.zh: 将水池视为城市基础设施：储存季节性水源有助于干旱环境中的城市生活。

alt.zh: 陡坡石金字塔与小型入口礼拜堂成群分布于干旱景观。

caption.en: Pyramids at Meroë in Sudan, photographed in 2001. These royal burial monuments belong to the history of Kush.
caption.zh: 2001年拍摄的苏丹麦罗埃金字塔。这些王室墓葬纪念建筑属于库施历史。

interpretation.en: Their steep profiles and adjoining chapels invite comparison with other Nile monuments while keeping Kush’s own royal tradition in view.
interpretation.zh: 陡峭轮廓与相邻礼拜堂既可与尼罗河其他古迹比较，也呈现库施自身的王室传统。

caption.en: The Great Bath in the foreground of a 2014 view of Mohenjo-daro’s excavated ruins.
caption.zh: 2014年摩亨佐达罗遗址照片中，前景为大浴池。

interpretation.en: Brick-lined water architecture makes the entry’s account of organized urban life concrete, without requiring a named king.
interpretation.zh: 砖砌水利建筑让条目中的城市组织具体可见，无须假定某位已知国王。

title.zh: 那烂陀的砖筑学习空间

alt.en: Low brick platforms and a larger ruined temple stand among grass and trees.
alt.zh: 低矮砖台与较大的寺庙遗迹分布在草地和树木之间。

caption.en: Temple 12 at Nalanda, photographed in 2023. Brick shrines formed part of a much larger monastic and scholastic complex.
caption.zh: 2023年拍摄的那烂陀第12号寺庙。砖筑圣殿是庞大寺院与教学建筑群的一部分。

interpretation.en: The surviving walls turn a history of learning into a question of space: study, residence and worship needed connected buildings.
interpretation.zh: 遗存墙体使学习史成为空间问题：研习、居住和礼拜需要相互连接的建筑。

alt.zh: 长条深色石柱交错堆叠，构成厚重墙体。

caption.en: Basalt masonry at Nan Madol, a ceremonial centre built on artificial islets near Pohnpei.
caption.zh: 南马都尔的玄武岩砌体；这处仪式中心建于波纳佩附近的人工小岛上。

interpretation.en: Stacked columns show how distinctive local materials supported large-scale island engineering.
interpretation.zh: 叠置石柱展示独特地方材料如何支撑大规模岛屿工程。

alt.en: A rounded stone stupa rises behind a carved gateway.
alt.zh: 圆顶石塔矗立在雕刻门楼之后。

caption.en: The Great Stupa at Sanchi, seen in a modern photograph. Its gateways and enclosure guide movement around the monument.
caption.zh: 现代照片中的桑吉大塔。门楼和围栏引导人们环绕佛塔行进。

interpretation.en: Look at the relationship between gate, path and dome: Buddhist worship shaped both architecture and movement.
interpretation.zh: 观察门、路径与圆顶的关系：佛教礼拜同时塑造了建筑和行进方式。

title.zh: 锡吉里耶的园林与岩山

alt.en: Looking down from Sigiriya’s rock, straight paths and rectangular garden pools recede through trees.
alt.zh: 从锡吉里耶岩顶俯瞰，笔直路径与矩形园池在树木之间向远处延伸。

caption.en: Gardens below Sigiriya’s rock, part of a royal landscape organized around water and elevation.
caption.zh: 锡吉里耶岩山下的园林，是围绕水与高差组织的王室景观的一部分。

interpretation.en: Read the gardens together with the summit: engineering below helped give meaning to royal height above.
interpretation.zh: 将园林与岩顶合看：下方工程与上方王室高地共同构成景观。

alt.en: A long straight avenue runs between stepped platforms toward a large pyramid.
alt.zh: 笔直长道穿过阶梯台基之间，通向大型金字塔。

caption.en: The Avenue of the Dead at Teotihuacan, a major axis within the city’s geometric plan.
caption.zh: 特奥蒂瓦坎亡者大道，是城市几何规划中的重要轴线。

interpretation.en: The view makes alignment and repeated building forms legible at the scale of a city.
interpretation.zh: 这一视角使城市尺度的轴线与重复建筑形式清晰可读。

alt.en: A tall tiered stone temple tower rises over a broad walled courtyard.
alt.zh: 高大层叠石塔耸立于宽阔围墙庭院之上。

caption.en: Brihadisvara temple at Thanjavur, commissioned by Rajaraja I in the early eleventh century and used for worship across later centuries.
caption.zh: 坦贾武尔布里哈迪斯瓦拉神庙，由罗阇罗阇一世于十一世纪初营建，后世持续用于礼拜。

interpretation.en: The tower’s scale opens a discussion of the builders, endowments and institutional resources behind a royal religious commission.
interpretation.zh: 塔体尺度引出对建造者、捐赠与机构资源的讨论，展现王室宗教工程背后的组织。

alt.en: A frontal view shows Temple I’s steep central stairway, stepped stone base and tall roof comb above trees.
alt.zh: 正面视角展示一号神庙陡峭的中央阶梯、层叠石基与高出树木的屋脊。

caption.en: Temple I at Tikal, within a Maya city of temples, palaces, plazas and residential districts.
caption.zh: 蒂卡尔一号神庙，所在玛雅城市还包括宫殿、广场和居住区。

interpretation.en: The temple is an anchor for reading the city, not a substitute for its many households and living Maya history.
interpretation.zh: 神庙是理解城市的定位点，不能代替众多住户与延续至今的玛雅历史。

alt.en: A young woman reaches into a leafy garden while pale saintly figures appear behind her.
alt.zh: 年轻女子伸手探向枝叶繁茂的花园，淡色圣徒形象浮现在她身后。

caption.en: Jules Bastien-Lepage painted this scene in 1879, centuries after Joan’s life. It imagines her encounter with saints in her parents’ garden.
caption.zh: 朱尔·巴斯蒂安-勒帕热于1879年绘制此画，比贞德生活的年代晚数百年。画中想象她在父母花园遇见圣徒的场景。

interpretation.en: The contrast between a closely observed garden and ghostly figures makes a later act of remembrance visible. The museum connects the painting to renewed interest in Joan after the Franco-Prussian War.
interpretation.zh: 细察入微的花园与幽影般人物形成对比，使后世纪念的方式清晰可见。博物馆将此画与普法战争后重新兴起的贞德崇敬相联系。

title.zh: 卡拉卡拉的官方帝王形象

alt.en: A marble head has close-cropped curls, a short beard, furrowed brows and a forcefully turned neck.
alt.zh: 大理石头像留短卷发和短须，双眉紧蹙，颈部有力地转向一侧。

caption.en: Roman marble portrait, 212–217 CE, made during Caracalla’s reign. The head belonged to a full statue; its closely cropped hair and beard project a military style.
caption.zh: 罗马大理石肖像，公元212至217年，制作于卡拉卡拉在位时。头像原属全身雕像，短发短须呈现军人风格。

interpretation.en: The citizenship edict came from an emperor whose authority was also communicated through sculpture. Examine the face as an official presentation of power, alongside the legal text discussed in the entry.
interpretation.zh: 发布公民权敕令的皇帝，也借雕塑传播权威。可将这张脸视作官方塑造的权力形象，与条目讨论的法律文本对读。

title.en: Rations for messengers in Ur III
title.zh: 乌尔第三王朝信使的口粮

alt.en: A small rectangular clay tablet is covered with horizontal rows of wedge-shaped writing.
alt.zh: 小块长方形泥板布满横排楔形文字。

caption.en: This tablet from Umma records beer, bread, oil and onions for messengers. Its internal date is year 1 of Ibbi-Sin, month 2, day 20, conventionally about 2028 BCE.
caption.zh: 这块来自温马的泥板记录给信使的啤酒、面包、油和洋葱。板上纪年为伊比辛元年二月二十日，通常约合公元前2028年。

interpretation.en: Empire appears here as provisions, quantities and a dated record. A palm-sized account reveals the routine support needed to move information between officials.
interpretation.zh: 帝国在这里表现为物资、数量和注明日期的账目。掌心大小的记录，显现官员之间传递信息所需的日常保障。

alt.en: A rounded square clay tablet carries closely packed lines of cuneiform across its face and edges.
alt.zh: 圆角方形泥板的正面与边缘，密布楔形文字。

caption.en: Old Assyrian letter, about the twentieth–nineteenth centuries BCE, probably from Kültepe. Ilabrat-bani writes to Amur-ili about textiles, clothing requests and travel.
caption.zh: 古亚述书信，约公元前二十至十九世纪，可能来自居尔特佩。伊拉布拉特巴尼致信阿穆尔伊利，谈到织品、衣物需求与旅行。

interpretation.en: The dense writing links long-distance trade to personal needs and household communication. The small tablet had to travel with people and goods.
interpretation.zh: 密集文字把远距离贸易与个人需求、家庭通信联系起来。这块小泥板，需要随着人员和货物一起移动。

title.en: Bukhara suzani: a design joined from strips
title.zh: 布哈拉苏扎尼：由布条拼合的图案

alt.en: Large red floral rosettes and curling stems fill an embroidered cover with a wide flowered border.
alt.zh: 绣制盖布上铺满红色大花盘与卷曲枝茎，四周围以宽阔花边。

caption.en: Early nineteenth-century suzani attributed to Bukhara, embroidered in silk on linen. Separate worked strips were joined to create a large furnishing textile.
caption.zh: 十九世纪初苏扎尼绣品，归于布哈拉，以丝线绣于亚麻布上。分别完成刺绣的布条拼合为大型室内织物。

interpretation.en: Follow a stem across a seam: changes in alignment or colour can reveal the shared work behind the finished design. This is the particular cover discussed in the entry.
interpretation.zh: 沿着枝茎跨过接缝，图案或颜色的变化可以显露成品背后的协作劳动。这正是条目所讨论的那件盖布。

title.zh: 手绘的科罗曼德尔棉布

alt.en: A long narrow cotton panel repeats elaborate red and blue floral forms against a pale ground.
alt.zh: 狭长棉布在浅色底面反复排列繁复的红蓝花卉图案。

caption.en: Coromandel Coast, first quarter of the eighteenth century. Specialist painters applied most of this repeat design freehand, using resist and mordant dyeing.
caption.zh: 科罗曼德尔海岸，十八世纪前四分之一。专业画工主要徒手绘制重复纹样，并使用防染与媒染工艺。

interpretation.en: Repetition does not necessarily mean mechanical printing. The cloth brings painters’ control of line and colour into a story of export demand; the museum identifies East India Company import as probable.
interpretation.zh: 重复纹样不一定意味着机械印花。这块布把画工控制线条与颜色的技艺带入出口贸易史；博物馆认为它可能由东印度公司输入欧洲。

title.en: Merian’s plants, colour and workshop practice
title.zh: 梅里安的植物、色彩与作坊实践

alt.en: Two flowering plant sprigs stand on pale vellum beside a small red beetle.
alt.zh: 浅色羊皮纸上绘两枝开花植物，旁边有一只小红甲虫。

caption.en: Maria Sibylla Merian, Study of Capers, Gorse, and a Beetle, 1693. Watercolour and white gouache on vellum, made in Amsterdam before her Suriname journey.
caption.zh: 玛丽亚·西比拉·梅里安，《刺山柑、荆豆与甲虫习作》，1693年。羊皮纸水彩与白色水粉，绘于阿姆斯特丹，早于她的苏里南之行。

interpretation.en: Merian reworked plant designs from an earlier print for a different collecting audience. The sheet connects close observation with the practical business of a family workshop; it is not a plate from her 1705 Suriname book.
interpretation.zh: 梅里安将早期版画中的植物设计重新安排，以面向不同的收藏者。这一画页把细致观察与家庭作坊经营相连，并非1705年苏里南著作中的图版。

title.zh: 伽利略肖像在印刷品中流传

alt.en: A bearded man appears in an oval frame surrounded by an elaborate engraved cartouche and lettering.
alt.zh: 有须男子位于椭圆框内，周围为精细雕版饰框与文字。

caption.en: Francesco Villamena’s engraved portrait of Galileo, 1623 state. The portrait was first commissioned for the 1613 book on sunspots and reused for Il Saggiatore in 1623.
caption.zh: 弗朗切斯科·维拉梅纳的伽利略雕版肖像，1623年版态。肖像最初为1613年的太阳黑子著作而作，1623年又用于《试金者》。

interpretation.en: Observation reached readers through books as well as instruments. Reusing a portrait plate shows how scientific authorship acquired a recognisable public face.
interpretation.zh: 观测成果不仅借仪器，也通过书籍抵达读者。肖像铜版的重复使用，显示科学作者如何获得公众熟悉的面貌。

alt.en: An engraved page combines a busy bookbinding workshop above with numbered tools and equipment below.
alt.zh: 雕版页上部是一间忙碌的装订作坊，下部排列带编号的工具与设备。

caption.en: The Met identifies this image as Volume 8, Plate 1, “Relieur”: procedures for binding a book. Its catalogue gives 1751–65 for the publication record, not a separately established date for this plate.
caption.zh: 大都会将此图标为第八卷第一图版“Relieur”：书籍装订工序。目录中的1751至1765年是出版记录的年代，并非单独确定的本图版制作日期。

interpretation.en: The book explains the labour needed to make books. Read the workplace scene together with the numbered tools to see how a craft was divided into teachable operations.
interpretation.zh: 这部书也解释制作书籍所需的劳动。把作坊场景与编号工具对读，可以看出一种手艺如何被拆解成可传授的操作。

alt.en: A profile engraving shows Martin Luther in a soft cap and monastic clothing above a Latin inscription.
alt.zh: 侧面雕版肖像中的马丁·路德戴软帽、着修士服，下方有拉丁文题记。

caption.en: Lucas Cranach the Elder, 1521, engraving. Luther appears as an Augustinian friar during the early years of the Reformation controversy.
caption.zh: 老卢卡斯·克拉纳赫，1521年，雕版画。宗教改革争论初期，路德以奥古斯丁会修士形象出现。

interpretation.en: A reproducible face could travel with arguments in print. The portrait shows the reformer four years after 1517, rather than illustrating the posting of the theses.
interpretation.zh: 可以复制的面孔能够与印刷论辩一同传播。这幅肖像表现的是1517年后四年的改革者，并非张贴论纲的场景。

title.en: A saint worn beside the face
title.zh: 佩在面庞旁的圣徒形象

alt.en: A round gold pendant hangs below a large loop, with an enamel saint and small geometric inlays on its face.
alt.zh: 圆形金吊饰垂在大环下，表面有珐琅圣徒与小型几何镶饰。

caption.en: Kyiv, eleventh–twelfth century. This temple pendant combines gold, cloisonné enamel and pearls with a Christian saint holding a martyr’s cross.
caption.zh: 基辅，十一至十二世纪。这件鬓饰以金、掐丝珐琅和珍珠制作，内有手持殉道十字架的基督教圣徒。

interpretation.en: Byzantine court fashion became locally made jewellery. An object worn near the face joined religious imagery to personal display in the princely world of Rus’.
interpretation.zh: 拜占庭宫廷风尚转化为本地制作的首饰。佩在脸旁的器物，在罗斯诸王公的世界中把宗教图像与个人展示结合起来。

title.zh: 在阿拜多斯发现的克尔马陶器

alt.en: A thin-walled beaker flares outward, with a polished red lower body and black rim and interior.
alt.zh: 薄壁杯向上敞开，下部为磨光红色，上缘与内部呈黑色。

caption.en: Classic Kerma beaker, about 1802–1640 BCE, excavated in Tomb 525 at Abydos in Egypt. Its colour zones required carefully controlled firing.
caption.zh: 经典克尔马陶杯，约公元前1802至1640年，出土于埃及阿拜多斯525号墓。分明色区需要精细控制烧制条件。

interpretation.en: This Nubian ceramic tradition appears in an Egyptian burial context. The find makes contact across the Nile region tangible while leaving the tomb owner’s identity uncertain.
interpretation.zh: 努比亚陶器传统出现在埃及墓葬中。发现地点使尼罗河区域间的联系具体可见，但墓主身份仍不确定。

title.en: Navoi’s poetry copied for later readers
title.zh: 为后世读者抄写的纳沃伊诗歌

alt.en: A manuscript painting shows a seated prince, dancers, musicians and attendants gathered in a courtyard.
alt.zh: 手稿绘画中，坐着的王子、舞者、乐师与侍从聚集在庭院里。

caption.en: Illustrated folio from a divan of Alisher Navoi, dated 1580 and attributed to Iran. Qasim Ali of Shiraz supplied the calligraphy; the painter is not named in the record.
caption.zh: 纳沃伊诗集绘画书页，纪年1580年，归于伊朗。书法由设拉子的卡西姆·阿里完成，目录未记画家姓名。

interpretation.en: Navoi died in 1501. This later feast scene shows the continuing copying and interpretation of his poetry, rather than a portrait of his own court or daily life.
interpretation.zh: 纳沃伊于1501年去世。这幅后来的宴饮图表现其诗歌持续被抄写、解读的历史，并非他本人宫廷或日常生活的肖像记录。

title.en: A silver vessel designed to whistle

alt.en: A silver beaker connects through a tube to a hollow seated monkey holding fruit to its mouth.
alt.zh: 银杯通过导管连接一只中空坐猴，猴子将果实举到嘴边。

caption.en: Chimú silversmiths, 1350–1470 CE. Twenty-four pieces of silver sheet form a double-chambered vessel whose internal whistle sounded as liquid displaced air.
caption.zh: 奇穆银匠，公元1350至1470年。二十四片银板组成双腔器皿，液体排挤空气时，内部哨体可以发声。

interpretation.en: Look for the connection between the two chambers: skilled metalwork made serving a drink into a sensory performance. The museum relates such vessels to elite feasts and rulership.
interpretation.zh: 留意两个腔体之间的连接：高超金工使饮酒成为有声音的表演。博物馆将此类器皿与精英宴饮和统治权联系起来。

title.en: A miniature Đông Sơn drum with four frogs
title.zh: 带四只蛙的东山文化小型鼓

alt.en: A small bronze drum has a broad decorated top, narrow waist and four raised frogs around its rim.
alt.zh: 小型铜鼓有宽阔纹饰鼓面、收窄腰部，鼓缘周围塑四只蛙。

caption.en: Vietnam, about 500 BCE–300 CE. The bronze miniature belongs to the Đông Sơn drum tradition and is only about ten centimetres high.
caption.zh: 越南，约公元前500年至公元300年。此小型铜鼓属于东山文化铜鼓传统，高度仅约十厘米。

interpretation.en: A small surviving object opens questions about casting, scale and exchange. Drums and models travelled widely, but the function of this particular miniature is not securely established.
interpretation.zh: 小小实物打开有关铸造、尺度与交换的问题。铜鼓及模型广泛流传，但这件小型鼓的具体用途尚不能确定。

alt.zh: 小型铜像直立，戴高冠，着贴身长衣，双手向前伸出。

caption.en: Standing Prajnaparamita, Thailand, thirteenth century. The Met classifies this bronze within the Sukhothai period.

title.en: A crowned Buddha in wood, lacquer and gold
title.zh: 木、漆与金构成的戴冠佛像

alt.en: A black-and-white photograph shows a standing Buddha with an elaborate pointed crown, long robe and one raised hand.
alt.zh: 黑白照片中的立佛戴精致尖冠，着长袍，一手举起。

caption.en: Myanmar, about the thirteenth–early fourteenth century. The Met identifies the wooden, lacquered and gilded sculpture as Pagan-period work.
caption.zh: 缅甸，约十三至十四世纪初。大都会将这件木雕漆金佛像归为蒲甘时期作品。

interpretation.en: Wood, lacquer and gilding required different kinds of skilled work. The broad object date extends beyond the court’s conventional political endpoint, illustrating the longer life of devotional traditions.
interpretation.zh: 木雕、髹漆与贴金需要不同技艺。器物的宽泛断代延伸至宫廷政治通常分期的终点之后，显示信仰艺术传统更长的生命。

alt.en: A narrow textile band repeats frontal figures holding staffs in alternating red, yellow, green and blue blocks.
alt.zh: 狭长织物带在红、黄、绿、蓝相间色块中反复绣出正面持杖人物。

caption.en: Garment-border fragment, Peru, fourth–third century BCE. Dense embroidery covers a plain-woven camelid-fibre foundation.
caption.zh: 服饰边饰残片，秘鲁，公元前四至三世纪。密集刺绣覆盖在骆驼科动物纤维的平纹底布上。

interpretation.en: Repeated figures change colour without losing their rhythm. Following the stitches brings the labour of making cloth into the entry’s account of clothing and burial.
interpretation.zh: 重复人物在保持节奏的同时变换颜色。沿针脚细看，可以把制布劳动带入条目关于服饰和墓葬的叙述。

caption.en: Lambayeque (Sicán), Peru, ninth–eleventh century. Gold and pigment formed an image used in funerary display.

interpretation.en: Thin metal could make a striking face through shaping, reflection and colour. The mask anchors the entry’s discussion of specialist craft without assigning an undocumented personal identity to its wearer.

alt.en: A crowded city square surrounds a tall decorated tree, with monumental buildings behind the gathering.
alt.zh: 拥挤城市广场上的人群围绕高大装饰树聚集，背后矗立大型建筑。

caption.en: Daniël Johannes Torman Kerkhoff, 1795 or later. The drawing represents celebrations in Dam Square on 4 March 1795, during the Batavian Revolution.
caption.zh: 丹尼尔·约翰内斯·托尔曼·克尔克霍夫，1795年或以后。画作表现巴达维亚革命期间，1795年3月4日水坝广场的庆典。

interpretation.en: A public square became a stage for a changed political order. This image marks the Dutch Republic’s transition, rather than the sixteenth-century beginning of its independence.
interpretation.zh: 公共广场成为展示政治秩序变化的舞台。图像对应荷兰共和国终结时的转型，并非十六世纪独立过程的开端。

title.en: A Qajar artist records a Sasanian relief
title.zh: 卡扎尔画家记录萨珊浮雕

alt.en: An ink drawing outlines a mounted ruler and figures approaching him within a rocky relief setting.
alt.zh: 水墨线描勾勒岩壁浮雕中的骑马君王，以及向他靠近的人物。

caption.en: Lutf-Ali Shirazi’s drawing of 1812 records the Sasanian relief of Shapur I and the Roman emperor Valerian at Naqsh-i Rustam. The drawing and the ancient monument have different dates.
caption.zh: 卢特夫·阿里·设拉子1812年的画作记录纳克什鲁斯塔姆的萨珊浮雕，主题为沙普尔一世与罗马皇帝瓦勒良。画作与古代纪念物的年代不同。

interpretation.en: The mounted king’s scale and the positions of other figures communicate hierarchy. Read this as a later record of Sasanian royal imagery, not a surviving third-century drawing or an eyewitness battle scene.
interpretation.zh: 骑马君王的尺度与其他人物的位置表达等级。此图是对萨珊王权图像的后世记录，不是三世纪原画，也不是战役现场写生。

title.en: A winged guardian at an Assyrian palace
title.zh: 亚述宫殿的有翼守护神

alt.en: A monumental human-headed winged lion combines a patterned beard, feathered wings and a powerful animal body.
alt.zh: 巨大的有人首有翼狮将纹理细密的胡须、羽翼与强壮兽身结合。

caption.en: Neo-Assyrian guardian from the palace of Ashurnasirpal II at Nimrud, about 883–859 BCE. The composite figure stood at a palace entrance.
caption.zh: 新亚述守护神，出自尼姆鲁德亚述纳西尔帕二世宫殿，约公元前883至859年。复合形象原立于宫殿入口。

interpretation.en: Architecture made power something visitors physically approached. The creature’s human head, animal body and wings join different capacities in a monumental protector.
interpretation.zh: 建筑使权力成为访客必须亲身走近的存在。人首、兽身和双翼把不同能力组合为巨大的守护者。

title.zh: 早期文字中的谷物计数

alt.en: A small clay tablet is divided into compartments containing drawn signs and round numerical impressions.
alt.zh: 小泥板分成数格，格内刻画符号，并压有圆形数字记号。

caption.en: Proto-cuneiform account, about 3100–2900 BCE, probably from Uruk. The museum interprets it as an account of grain deliveries and distributions, including barley and emmer.
caption.zh: 原始楔形文字账目，约公元前3100至2900年，可能来自乌鲁克。博物馆将其解释为谷物收发记录，涉及大麦与二粒小麦。

interpretation.en: Compare the drawn signs with the circular quantity marks. Early writing joined pictures, numbers and layout to store economic information; some details of these texts remain difficult to read.
interpretation.zh: 比较刻画符号与圆形数量记号：早期书写结合图形、数字和版面保存经济信息，这类文本的部分细节仍难以解读。

title.en: An Ilkhanid tile names the Fourteen Infallibles
title.zh: 伊儿汗国瓷砖上的十四位无谬者

alt.en: A turquoise-glazed tile forms a pointed niche framed by raised calligraphy and slender columns.
alt.zh: 绿松石色釉砖以凸起书法与细柱围成尖拱龛形。

caption.en: Dated 712 AH/1312–13 CE and attributed to Sultanabad, Iran. The molded tile invokes the Fourteen Infallibles within a mihrab-like design.
caption.zh: 纪年伊斯兰历712年，即公元1312至1313年，归于伊朗苏丹纳巴德。模制瓷砖以类似米哈拉布的龛形设计祈颂十四位无谬者。

interpretation.en: The inscription connects a decorative surface with Shi‘i religious commitments during Uljaitu’s reign. It gives a dated material example of the religious and artistic changes discussed in the entry.
interpretation.zh: 铭文将装饰表面与完者都时期的什叶派信仰相连，为条目讨论的宗教及艺术变化提供有明确年代的实物。

title.zh: 介于尼沙普尔与撒马尔罕之间的陶碗

alt.en: A pale, repaired bowl carries two red-and-dark vegetal designs linked by dots; cracks run across the surface.
alt.zh: 浅色修复陶碗内有两个红色与深色植物纹样，以圆点连接，表面可见裂缝。

caption.en: Tenth-century slip-painted earthenware, attributed to Nishapur in Iran or Samarqand in present-day Uzbekistan. The museum retains both possible origins.
caption.zh: 十世纪化妆土彩绘陶碗，归于伊朗尼沙普尔或今乌兹别克斯坦撒马尔罕；博物馆保留两种可能产地。

interpretation.en: The shared ceramic language makes links between Samanid cities visible. Its uncertain workshop location is itself a useful question about how styles and skills moved.
interpretation.zh: 共享的陶艺形式使萨曼城市间的联系可见。难以确定的作坊所在地，也提出风格与技艺如何流动的问题。

alt.zh: 铜佛盘腿坐于精致宝座上，双手举于胸前。

caption.en: Bihar, India, late ninth century, Pala period. The bronze figure with silver inlay is just over thirteen centimetres high.
caption.zh: 印度比哈尔，九世纪晚期，波罗时期。嵌银铜像高约十三厘米。

interpretation.en: The small sculpture brings Buddhist image-making into the political history of eastern India. Its crafted throne and teaching gesture focus attention on devotion and skilled production.
interpretation.zh: 小型雕像将佛教造像带入东印度政治史。精制宝座与说法手势，把注意力引向信仰实践和专业制作。

alt.en: A richly carved four-armed deity stands between two smaller figures under an arch of miniature divine forms.
alt.zh: 繁复雕刻的四臂神像立于两尊小像之间，上方拱饰布满微型神祇形象。

caption.en: Dasoja of Balligrama, first quarter of the twelfth century, Karnataka, probably Belur. An inscription names the sculptor of this Keshava form of Vishnu.
caption.zh: 巴利格拉马的达索贾，十二世纪前四分之一，卡纳塔克，可能为贝鲁尔。铭文记下这尊凯沙瓦形毗湿奴像的雕刻者姓名。

interpretation.en: A named craftsperson enters a history often organized around royal patrons. Follow the four attributes, attendants and small surrounding figures to see how a temple image coordinated many layers of meaning.
interpretation.zh: 在常以王室赞助者为中心的历史中，一位有名有姓的工匠出现了。细看四件持物、侍从与周围小像，可以理解寺庙造像如何组织多层意义。

interpretation.zh: 近景显示城墙是砌筑和维护的累积，不只是围绕城市的一条线。

context.en: The Ban Zhao leaf is one part of the 1799 album commissioned by Cao Zhenxiu and painted by Gai Qi.
context.zh: 班昭图是1799年曹贞秀委托改琦绘制的画册中的一页。

context.en: This is the Chuquibamba star-patterned tunic discussed in the story, Met 33.149.100.
context.zh: 这就是故事讨论的丘基班巴星纹织衣，大都会藏品号33.149.100。

context.en: This is the terracotta column surround discussed in the story, Met 1992.151.
context.zh: 这就是故事讨论的陶制柱饰，大都会藏品号1992.151。

context.en: This actual Persepolis palace relief makes the entry’s discussion of staged imperial order concrete: a Median figure joins a formal procession. It dates to about 405–359 BCE, not the reign of Cyrus or the first building campaign under Darius.
context.zh: 这块真实的波斯波利斯宫殿浮雕，以参加正式行列的米底人物，使本条关于帝国秩序展示的讨论具体化。它约制作于公元前405至359年，并非居鲁士在位或大流士最初营建时期。

context.en: The portrait identifies Queen Liliʻuokalani, whose government was overthrown in 1893 and whose protest continued afterward. The sitting was around 1891; the print’s 1916 inscription is later. It does not depict the overthrow itself.
context.zh: 肖像呈现1893年政府被推翻、此后继续抗议的利留卡拉尼女王。拍摄约在1891年，照片的1916年题字为后加，并非政变现场图。

context.en: Justinian’s name and Roman titles on this 521 consular ivory give material form to the inherited official traditions discussed in the legal-compilation entry. The object predates his imperial reign and the 529–534 compilation; it contains no law text.
context.zh: 521年执政官象牙板上的查士丁尼姓名与罗马官衔，使法律编纂条目所述继承的官职传统具有物质形式。它早于其帝王统治及529至534年编纂，不含法律正文。

context.en: The ivory names Justinian, the patron who ordered Hagia Sophia rebuilt. Its 521 consular display offers an earlier example of his public titles, before the church’s 532–537 rebuilding. It is neither architectural fabric nor a view of the church.
context.zh: 象牙板铭记下令重建圣索菲亚教堂的赞助者查士丁尼；521年执政官身份展示，早于532至537年教堂重建。它既非教堂建筑构件，也非教堂景观图。

context.en: Douglass spoke at the 1848 convention, and its report was printed at his North Star office. This portrait from about 1879 identifies the participant and publisher at a later stage of life, not his appearance at the meeting.
context.zh: 道格拉斯在1848年大会发言，大会报告也在其《北极星报》印刷所印制。这张约1879年的肖像呈现参与者与出版者晚年的面貌，并非会场时的样貌。

context.en: The 1776 Declaration supplied a rhetorical model for the 1848 Declaration of Sentiments. Viewing the earlier document invites comparison of whose equality each declaration claimed. This parchment is the Declaration of Independence, not the convention’s own statement.
context.zh: 1776年《独立宣言》为1848年《感伤宣言》提供修辞范本。观看较早文献，可比较两份宣言分别主张谁的平等。这张羊皮纸是《独立宣言》，而非大会自身声明。

context.en: Tagore founded the Santiniketan school in 1901. His approximately 1909 portrait identifies the educator behind the experiment during its early development, before Visva-Bharati’s 1921 foundation. It shows the founder, not the campus or a teaching session.
context.zh: 泰戈尔于1901年创办圣蒂尼克坦学校。约1909年的肖像呈现教育实验早期的创办者，早于1921年维斯瓦—巴拉蒂成立；它展示人物，并非校园或授课场景。

context.en: The Emancipation Proclamation was publicly read at Camp Saxton on 1 January 1863. This archival page connects the gathering to the named legal document; it is not the particular copy used at the camp or a visual record of the celebration.
context.zh: 1863年1月1日，萨克斯顿营地公开宣读《解放宣言》。这张档案书页将集会与该法律文献联系起来，但并非营地当时使用的那份副本，也非庆典图像记录。

context.en: The entry contrasts palace representations of order with administrative accounts. This Persepolis processional relief supplies the palace side of that comparison. It dates to about 405–359 BCE, later than the 509–494 BCE Fortification tablets, and is not a ration record.
context.zh: 本条将宫殿表现的秩序与行政账目对读；这块波斯波利斯行列浮雕提供宫殿一侧的比较材料。它约制作于公元前405至359年，晚于前509至494年的城防泥板，并非配给记录。

context.en: The surviving proclamation page is a primary document of Lincoln’s January 1863 action discussed in the biography. Its specified rebellious territories and exceptions help distinguish wartime emancipation from nationwide abolition.
context.zh: 存世宣言书页，是传记所述林肯1863年1月行动的原始文献。其指定叛乱地区及例外条款，有助于区分战时解放与全国废奴。

context.en: A Tang copy of the preface composed for the Orchid Pavilion gathering of 353.
context.zh: 353年兰亭雅集所作序文的唐代摹本。

context.en: The celebrated preface survives through later copies, including this Tang sheet attributed to Feng Chengsu.
context.zh: 著名序文经后世摹本流传，其中包括这件传为冯承素所作的唐摹本。

context.en: Chen Hongshou’s Returning Home imagines the poet whose resignation is described here. Its 1650 image belongs to the later reception of that choice.
context.zh: 陈洪绶《归去来》描绘本条辞官的诗人；1650年的画作属于后世对这一选择的理解。

context.en: Qu Yuan, the courtier in this entry, appears as a remembered poet in this Ming encyclopedia.
context.zh: 本条中的朝臣屈原，在这部明代百科图书中被塑造成后人记忆中的诗人。

context.en: The Ming print gives a later face to the poet whose exile and writing anchor this entry.
context.zh: 明代版画为本条放逐与创作故事的主角提供后世诗人形象。

context.en: A Yuan portrait of the author of Spring View, made centuries after the poem’s wartime setting.
context.zh: 《春望》作者的元代肖像，比诗中战乱背景晚数百年。

context.en: Du Fu in a Yuan portrait scroll, accompanying the story of his early Mount Tai poem.
context.zh: 元代立轴中的杜甫，与他早年泰山诗作的故事相联系。

context.en: This Yuan portrait of Du Fu pairs with the Song painting of Li Bai: two later images of poets who travelled together in 744–745.
context.zh: 这幅元代杜甫像与宋代李白图相对照：两位744至745年同游诗人的后世形象。

context.en: The retrospective scroll introduces Du Fu, whose family losses and official disappointments shaped his writing.
context.zh: 后世画卷呈现杜甫；家难与仕途失意塑造了他的写作。

context.en: A later portrait of the poet remembered through the Chengdu cottage and its poems.
context.zh: 后世杜甫像，使成都草堂及诗歌所纪念的诗人可见。

context.en: The Yuan portrait accompanies Du Fu’s Kuizhou years and the poems associated with them.
context.zh: 元代肖像与杜甫夔州时期及相关诗作相联系。

context.en: A commemorative portrait of the poet whose final travels are described here.
context.zh: 这幅纪念性肖像呈现本条晚年行旅中的诗人。

context.en: The Yuan album names Meng Ke, or Mencius, whose dialogue with King Hui contrasts profit and humane rule.
context.zh: 元代册页题名孟轲，即与梁惠王讨论利与仁义的孟子。

context.en: A Yuan image of Mencius as an honored teacher, linked here to his arguments about humane government.
context.zh: 元代孟子尊师形象，与本条讨论仁政的思想相联系。

context.en: The photographed scroll transcribes the Pipa Song named in this entry, showing the Tang poem’s later Ming calligraphic life.
context.zh: 照片中的手卷书写本条《琵琶行》，呈现唐诗在明代书法中的延续。

context.en: Jiang Xun’s later painting identifies Li Qingzhao, the collector and writer named here; flowers express her literary afterlife rather than inventorying the Qingzhou collection.
context.zh: 姜壎后世画作标识本条收藏者、词人李清照；花枝表达其文学接受史，而非罗列青州藏品。

context.en: The Qing painting commemorates Li Qingzhao, the writer named in this Jinhua episode, rather than illustrating a specific visit to Bayong Tower.
context.zh: 清代画作追怀本条金华经历中的李清照，并非描绘某次八咏楼之游。

context.en: The Song image commemorates the emperor installed after the fall of the Lü clan, showing the ideal of a ruler who hears advice.
context.zh: 宋代图像纪念吕氏覆亡后即位的汉文帝，呈现君主纳谏的理想。

context.en: The enthroned ruler is the Yongle emperor, who made Beijing the principal Ming capital.
context.zh: 宝座上的君主是永乐帝，他将北京定为明朝的主要都城。

context.en: The formal imperial image presents Zhu Di as sovereign after the Jingnan forces took Nanjing and he ascended the throne.
context.zh: 正式御容表现靖难军攻入南京、朱棣即位之后的皇帝身份。

context.en: Lin Zexu is the commissioner who supervised the destruction of confiscated opium at Humen.
context.zh: 林则徐是主持在虎门销毁所缴鸦片的钦差大臣。

context.en: Sima Guang is the historian at the center of this entry on compiling the Zizhi Tongjian in Luoyang.
context.zh: 司马光是此条目中在洛阳编纂《资治通鉴》的核心史家。

context.en: The portrait introduces Sima Guang as a participant in the correspondence with Wang Anshi over the New Policies.
context.zh: 此像呈现与王安石通过书信讨论新法的司马光。

context.en: The seated sovereign is Zhao Kuangyin, the military leader who became Song emperor after the Chenqiao mutiny.
context.zh: 端坐的君主是赵匡胤，即陈桥兵变后建立宋朝的军事首领。

context.en: The portrait identifies Emperor Yang, whose government ordered the Yongji Canal connecting the Yellow River with Zhuo Commandery.
context.zh: 图中人物为隋炀帝，其政府下令开凿连接黄河与涿郡的永济渠。

context.en: The Yuan album commemorates Temüjin, who took the title Genghis Khan as the Mongol political order was consolidated in 1206.
context.zh: 元代帝像册纪念铁木真；1206年蒙古政治秩序整合时，他取得成吉思汗称号。

context.en: The dynasty’s portrait of Genghis Khan anchors the entry’s opening discussion of unification in 1206 and the conquests that followed.
context.zh: 王朝绘制的成吉思汗像，与条目开篇讨论的1206年统一及随后征服相联系。

context.en: The imperial album portrait identifies Kublai, who proclaimed the dynastic name Great Yuan in 1271.
context.zh: 帝王像册中的人物为忽必烈，他于1271年定国号为“大元”。

context.en: The Qing ancestral portrait commemorates Nurhaci, who established the Later Jin khanate at Hetu Ala.
context.zh: 清代祖先御容纪念在赫图阿拉建立后金汗国的努尔哈赤。

context.en: Hong Taiji’s imperial dress connects directly to the proclamation of Qing and his assumption of the emperor’s title at Shengjing.
context.zh: 皇太极的帝王朝服，与他在盛京称帝并定国号为清的事件直接相连。

context.en: This court portrait identifies the Yongzheng emperor, under whose rule the Grand Council emerged as a central decision-making institution.
context.zh: 宫廷御容呈现雍正帝；其统治时期形成了作为中枢决策机构的军机处。

context.en: The later photograph identifies Li Hongzhang, one of the officials named in the foundation of the Jiangnan Arsenal.
context.zh: 较晚拍摄的照片呈现李鸿章，他是条目所述创办江南制造总局的官员之一。

context.en: Li Hongzhang, photographed in 1896, was the Qing negotiator who signed the Chefoo Convention two decades earlier.
context.zh: 1896年照片中的李鸿章，是二十年前签订《烟台条约》的清方谈判代表。

context.en: The 1875 portrait shows Zuo Zongtang, whose earlier memorial launched the Fuzhou shipbuilding and naval-education project.
context.zh: 1875年照片呈现左宗棠；此前他的奏请促成福州造船与海军教育事业。

context.en: The later printed portrait identifies Fan Zhongyan, a leader of the Qingli reforms named in this entry.
context.zh: 后世版画标识此条目所述庆历新政主持者范仲淹。

context.en: The portrait commemorates Fan Zhongyan, author of the Memorial to Yueyang Tower discussed here.
context.zh: 此像纪念本条目所述《岳阳楼记》的作者范仲淹。

context.en: This later artistic portrait identifies Xiang Yu, the commander associated here with the victory at Julu.
context.zh: 这幅后世艺术肖像呈现条目中巨鹿战役的统帅项羽。

context.en: Xiang Yu is one of the named leaders of the Jiangdong uprising; the portrait shows his later artistic reputation.
context.zh: 项羽是条目点名的江东起事领袖之一；肖像呈现他的后世艺术形象。

context.en: The 1918 reproduction identifies Zeng Guofan, the organizer of the Xiang Army discussed in this entry.
context.zh: 1918年刊载的肖像呈现本条目所述湘军组织者曾国藩。

context.en: The printed portrait names Zeng Guofan, one of the Xiang Army leaders in this account of Tianjing’s fall.
context.zh: 印刷肖像题名曾国藩，他是此处天京陷落叙述所提及的湘军领袖之一。

context.en: The illustrated narrative’s Wang Mang is the ruler who proclaimed the Xin dynasty in this entry.
context.zh: 通俗叙事中的王莽像对应本条目中建立新朝的统治者。

context.en: The hostile later portrait introduces Wang Mang, whose land and currency policies are the subject of this entry.
context.zh: 带有贬斥文字的后世肖像呈现此条目土地与币制政策的推行者王莽。

context.en: Gu Jianlong’s later painting commemorates Yu Qian, the minister who directed Beijing’s defense.
context.zh: 顾见龙的后世画像纪念指挥北京保卫战的大臣于谦。

context.en: The commemorative portrait identifies Yu Qian, whose execution forms part of this account of Yingzong’s restoration.
context.zh: 纪念像标识于谦，他的遇害是此处明英宗复辟叙述的一部分。

context.en: The Ming portrait depicts Ban Chao, who dispatched Gan Ying in the mission discussed here.
context.zh: 明代画像呈现班超，即条目所述派遣甘英出使的人物。

context.en: This later standing portrait commemorates Ban Chao, whose final return to Luoyang is the subject of the entry.
context.zh: 这幅后世立像纪念本条目叙述晚年返回洛阳的班超。

context.en: The album commemorates Han Yu, whose memorial against the Buddha relic led to the exile described here.
context.zh: 像册纪念韩愈；此条目叙述他因谏迎佛骨而遭贬谪。

context.en: The traveler’s costume in this later portrait offers a visual reading of the poet whose Hanzhong journey is described here.
context.zh: 后世肖像中的行旅装束，为条目叙述汉中经历的诗人陆游提供视觉解读。

context.en: This Qing portrait remembers Lu You, the poet whose final testament To My Sons is discussed in the entry.
context.zh: 这幅清代画像纪念陆游，条目讨论他的绝笔诗《示儿》。

context.en: The later book portrait commemorates Wen Tianxiang, the examination candidate named in this entry.
context.zh: 后世图传纪念此条目中参加殿试的文天祥。

context.en: The 1829 portrait belongs to the later remembrance of Wen Tianxiang’s captivity, poetry and death described here.
context.zh: 1829年的肖像属于对文天祥被囚、作诗与遇害经历的后世纪念。

context.en: The genealogy commemorates Shen Kuo, the author of Dream Pool Essays named in this entry.
context.zh: 族谱纪念本条目所述《梦溪笔谈》作者沈括。

context.en: This Tang manuscript preserves part of the Shiji, the work whose composition by Sima Qian is discussed here.
context.zh: 此唐写本保存《史记》的一部分，条目讨论司马迁撰写该书的经历。

context.en: The photographed observatory and shadow scale are the Gaocheng measuring installation named in this account of the Shoushi calendar.
context.zh: 照片中的观星台与测影长尺，正是此处《授时历》叙述点名的告成观测设施。

context.en: The Ming portrait commemorates Zhang Liang, the adviser honored with the title Marquis of Liu in this entry.
context.zh: 明代画像纪念此条目中受封留侯的谋臣张良。

context.en: This later portrait identifies Zhang Liang, one of the advisers named in the account of the Hongmen banquet.
context.zh: 此后世画像呈现鸿门宴叙述点名的谋臣之一张良。

context.en: The kendi’s spout and handleless form make the entry’s discussion of porcelain for Asian drinking practices concrete.
context.zh: 军持的流与无柄器形，使条目有关瓷器适应亚洲饮水习惯的讨论具体可见。

context.en: The right-hand portrait commemorates Guo Ziyi, the Tang commander named in the recovery of the two capitals.
context.zh: 右页肖像纪念收复两京叙述中点名的唐军统帅郭子仪。

context.en: Han Xin, shown at left in the later album, is the commander named in this account of Jingxing.
context.zh: 后世像册左页的韩信，是此井陉战役叙述中点名的统帅。

context.en: The facing portraits name Han Xin and Xiao He, both central figures in the account of Han Xin’s execution.
context.zh: 对开肖像题名韩信与萧何，两人均为韩信被杀叙述中的核心人物。

context.en: Ouyang Xiu sent this surviving letter from his retirement at Yingzhou, directly connecting the document with the place and life stage in this entry.
context.zh: 欧阳修退居颍州期间寄出此存世尺牍，直接连接条目所述地点与人生阶段。

context.en: The book portrait identifies Cao Cao, whose court politics and military provisioning are the subject of this biography.
context.zh: 书中肖像标识本传主角曹操；本传重点是他控制朝廷与组织军粮的实践。

entryTitle.en: Cao Cao · Grain, armies and the Han court
entryTitle.zh: 曹操 · 粮食、军队与汉廷

entrySummary.en: Cao Cao's power grew from a practical problem: armies could not survive without grain, and authority could not rest on victories alone. In 196 he brought the Han emperor's court to Xu and promoted agricultural colonies to provision his forces. This combined control of the court with a claim to act in the dynasty's name. At Guandu, attacks on Yuan Shao's supplies helped break a rival coalition. Expansion southward then met an alliance led by Sun Quan and Liu Bei at Red Cliffs. The setback left several centers of power in place. Reading his career through food, appointments and alliances makes it more intelligible than treating him as either a flawless strategist or a single villain.
entrySummary.zh: 曹操的权力建立在实际难题之上：军队离不开粮食，权威也不能只靠胜仗。196年，他将汉帝朝廷迁到许县，并推行屯田，为军队提供供给。控制朝廷与以汉朝名义行事，成为相互支撑的政治手段。官渡之战中，攻击袁绍粮运帮助他击破敌方联盟。随后向南扩张，却在赤壁遇到孙权与刘备的联合抵抗，战后多方势力继续并存。从粮食、官职与联盟来理解曹操，比把他写成无所不能的谋略家或单一反派，更能解释其成败。

context.en: This is the Cao Cao who besieged Lü Bu at Xiapi. The book portrait depicts the commander, not the flooding of the city.

entryTitle.en: Liu Bei · Building a state from shifting alliances
entryTitle.zh: 刘备 · 在变化的联盟中建国

entrySummary.en: Liu Bei moved through the fractured Han world by gathering followers and negotiating with stronger powers. Alliance with Sun Quan checked Cao Cao in 208, but cooperation did not settle their competing claims to Jingzhou. In the west, Liu Zhang invited him into Yi Province; their partnership became a war that ended with Liu Bei taking Chengdu. He proclaimed himself emperor in 221, presenting his state as a continuation of Han after Cao Pi's accession. An attack on his former ally Sun Quan then ended in defeat at Yiling. His final arrangements entrusted the young Liu Shan to Zhuge Liang and Li Yan. The career reveals how promises of restoration could coexist with territorial ambition and unstable alliances.
entrySummary.zh: 刘备在汉末分裂的局势中聚集追随者，与强势力量周旋。208年，他与孙权联合阻止曹操，但合作没有解决双方对荆州的竞争。向西发展时，刘璋邀请他进入益州，合作却转为战争，最终由刘备占领成都。221年，曹丕称帝之后，他也登基，以延续汉朝为建国理由。随后进攻旧盟友孙权，却在夷陵战败。临终时，他把年幼继承人刘禅托付给诸葛亮与李严。这段经历显示，恢复旧朝的政治承诺，如何与争夺领土、维持不稳固联盟同时存在。

entryTitle.en: Zhuge Liang · Administration behind a strategist’s fame
entryTitle.zh: 诸葛亮 · 谋略名声背后的治理

entrySummary.en: Zhuge Liang's work joined diplomacy, taxation, military supply and political counsel. He helped secure cooperation with Sun Quan, then supported Liu Bei's government at Chengdu. After Liu Bei died, he became the central administrator under Liu Shan and pursued campaigns intended to challenge Wei. Supply remained a persistent problem: the final campaign included soldiers farming near the Wei River to sustain a longer presence. The first northern expedition had already shown the consequences of failed command at Jieting. His memorials connect loyalty with responsibility for results. The annotated Sanguozhi also rejects some spectacular tales later attached to him. The historical official is most interesting where plans encounter distance, resources and other people's decisions.
entrySummary.zh: 诸葛亮的工作横跨外交、赋税、军粮与政治劝谏。他帮助促成与孙权的合作，又在成都支持刘备政权。刘备死后，他成为刘禅朝廷的主要执政者，并通过北方战役挑战魏国。供给始终是难题，最后一次出兵时，他安排军士在渭水附近耕作，以便长期驻扎。此前第一次北伐的街亭失利，已经显露指挥失误的后果。他的表文把忠诚与承担成败责任联系起来。《三国志》注还驳斥了某些附会于他的神奇故事。把计划放回距离、资源和其他人的选择之中，才更能看到这位历史人物。

entryTitle.en: Zhu Yuanzhang: rebuilding institutions and concentrating authority
entryTitle.zh: 朱元璋：重建制度与集中权力

entrySummary.en: Zhu Yuanzhang founded the Ming in 1368 and pursued a government that reached from the emperor’s court into village registration and local schools. Early measures established county granaries and promoted Confucian education. The lijia system introduced in 1381 organized households for administrative obligations, making local communities part of the state’s machinery. These institution-building projects accompanied an increasingly concentrated form of rule. The purge of Hu Weiyong in 1380 and the abolition of the chief minister’s position drew more decisions toward the emperor. His reign therefore links rebuilding after dynastic conflict with coercion and political suspicion. Schools and registers tell one part of that story; the destruction of officials and their networks tells another.
entrySummary.zh: 朱元璋1368年建立明朝，推动一种从皇帝朝廷延伸到乡村登记和地方学校的治理。早期措施兴设县级粮仓、推广儒学教育；1381年实行的里甲制度，把户籍与行政义务组织起来，使地方社区进入国家运转体系。这些制度营建伴随权力进一步集中。1380年胡惟庸案及丞相职位的废除，使更多决策直接归于皇帝。他的统治把王朝战乱后的重建与强制、政治猜忌联系起来：学校和簿册讲述其中一面，官员及其关系网络遭摧毁又呈现另一面。

entryTitle.en: Taizong: advice, conquest and imperial authority
entryTitle.zh: 唐太宗：纳谏、征服与皇权

entrySummary.en: Li Shimin became Emperor Taizong in 626 after helping his father establish Tang rule. His government expanded imperial power through campaigns as well as administration. Yet the advice he prepared for his heir in 648 turns attention to a different problem: how should a ruler hear criticism and choose the people who govern? The text presents self-restraint and attention to counsel as duties of kingship. It is a statement of governing ideals by an emperor, with a particular audience and purpose. Placed beside the career of his general Li Jing, it shows how military success and the language of responsible rule worked together in the early Tang court.
entrySummary.zh: 李世民帮助父亲建立唐朝后，于626年即帝位，是为唐太宗。战争与行政建设共同扩展了皇权，但他648年为继承者撰写的训诫，把注意力转向另一问题：君主应如何听取批评、选择治理国家的人？文中把节制自身与接受谏言视为君主的责任。这是一位皇帝面向特定读者表达的治国理想，具有明确的写作目的。与将领李靖的经历相对读，可以看到早唐朝廷如何把军事成就与负责治国的语言结合起来。

entryTitle.en: Sun Quan · Holding the lower Yangzi together
entryTitle.zh: 孙权 · 经营长江下游

entrySummary.en: Sun Quan inherited his brother Sun Ce's position in 200, but the territories and commanders he inherited did not form a settled kingdom. Building authority meant retaining experienced officers, negotiating with local elites and using force against communities beyond effective control. At Red Cliffs, he backed resistance to Cao Cao and cooperation with Liu Bei. Their alliance later fractured over Jingzhou, before further diplomacy restored cooperation against Wei. Sun Quan's imperial proclamation in 229 gave these regional arrangements a dynastic name: Wu. His story shifts attention from a single famous battle to the political work that kept a southern state operating among powerful neighbors, competing officials and communities with their own interests.
entrySummary.zh: 200年，孙权继承兄长孙策的地位，但接手的土地与将领并不构成一个已经稳定的王国。他需要留住有经验的军政人员，与地方精英合作，也对控制范围之外的群体动用武力。赤壁战前，他支持抵抗曹操，并与刘备联合。后来双方因荆州决裂，又通过外交重新合作抗魏。229年称帝，使这些区域性的经营拥有“吴”的王朝名号。他的经历把视线从一场著名战役移向持续的政治工作：如何在强邻、相互竞争的官员及各有诉求的地方群体之间，维持一个南方政权。

entryTitle.en: Sima Yi · From Wei commander to family power
entryTitle.zh: 司马懿 · 从魏臣到家族权力

entrySummary.en: Sima Yi served the Cao-Wei state before his family displaced it. Campaigns and court appointments gave him authority across military and civil affairs. In 238 he conquered the Gongsun regime in Liaodong; the Jin history records extensive killing after Xiangping fell, alongside its praise of his generalship. The decisive move at the center came in 249, when he seized control while Cao Shuang accompanied the emperor to the Gaoping tombs. Promises of retirement were followed by executions. Further repression secured his position before his death in 251. He did not reign as emperor during his lifetime. The imperial title used by the Jinshu belongs to the dynasty his descendants later founded and shapes its retrospective account.
entrySummary.zh: 司马懿先为曹魏效力，后来其家族取而代之。战役与朝廷任命使他掌握横跨军政的权力。238年，他征服辽东公孙氏政权；《晋书》在赞扬统兵能力的同时，也记载襄平陷落后的大规模杀戮。249年，曹爽陪皇帝谒高平陵时，他在京城夺取控制权。许以免官退居的安排，随后转成诛杀。进一步镇压反对力量后，他于251年去世。司马懿生前并未当皇帝，《晋书》所用帝号来自其后人建立王朝后的追尊，也影响了史书回顾其生涯的方式。

entryTitle.en: Yue Fei: a Song commander and the changing meaning of loyalty
entryTitle.zh: 岳飞：宋朝将领与忠诚含义的变化

entrySummary.en: Yue Fei entered the Song army in 1122 and rose through warfare against the Jurchen Jin and other armed opponents. His military service belonged to a divided political world in which the Southern Song court had to decide between continued fighting and negotiated survival. Recall and imprisonment in 1141 ended his command; he was executed the following year. Later temples, stories and political movements made him an enduring figure of loyalty. Historian Yue Du emphasizes that the state he served was the Song dynasty, while modern readers have given that loyalty changing national meanings. Keeping the commander beside his later reputation helps explain both a twelfth-century conflict and the uses of its memory.
entrySummary.zh: 岳飞1122年进入宋军，在对女真金朝及其他武装力量的战争中升任统帅。他所处的政治世界已经分裂，南宋朝廷需要在继续作战与议和求存之间作出选择。1141年被召回并入狱，结束了他的统军生涯，次年被处死。后来的祠庙、故事与政治活动不断把他塑造成忠诚典范。历史学者Yue Du强调，岳飞所效忠的国家是宋朝，而现代读者又为这种忠诚赋予不同的民族国家含义。将将领与后世声誉并读，有助于同时理解十二世纪冲突与历史记忆的用途。

entryTitle.en: Mud becomes a path: Su Shi and West Lake
entryTitle.zh: 湖泥成为长堤：苏轼与西湖

entrySummary.en:
Su Shi returned to govern Hangzhou in 1089. The West Lake Museum dates a major dredging project to 1090: material removed from the lake helped form the causeway later named after him. Six bridges interrupted the long embankment.

The History of Song connects his work with water supply and transport as well as the lake. What visitors admire as scenery also belongs to the history of maintaining a city. Its beauty emerged through repeated human work, not an untouched landscape.
entrySummary.zh:
1089年，苏轼再任杭州知州。西湖博物馆将一次大规模疏浚系于1090年：从湖中清出的泥土被用于筑堤，后来这条长堤以他命名。六座桥分布在长堤上。

《宋史》将这些工程同供水、运输以及湖泊联系起来。游人欣赏的景色，也是城市维护史的一部分。它的美来自反复的人力经营，并非从未改变的天然景观。

entryTitle.en: Qin: building an imperial afterlife
entryTitle.zh: 秦：建造帝国的地下世界

entrySummary.en: The first Qin emperor’s burial complex combined a large mound, planned enclosures and pits containing terracotta soldiers, horses and other objects. Construction began before the unification of China in 221 BCE. The surviving figures and weapons are evidence of military organisation and specialised production, while the overall layout echoes an imperial capital. A burial monument can therefore be read as evidence about the labour, authority and ambitions of the living.
entrySummary.zh: 秦始皇陵把巨大封土、规划整齐的围墙和兵马俑等陪葬坑组合成地下世界。工程在公元前221年统一之前已经开始。陶俑与兵器反映军事组织和专业化制作，整体布局则呼应帝国都城。观察一座陵墓，也能了解生者社会中的劳动组织、权力和愿望。

entryTitle.en: Yan Zhenqing: public duty and private mourning
entryTitle.zh: 颜真卿：公职与家难

entrySummary.en: Yan Zhenqing’s calligraphy preserves more than an admired style. The draft he wrote in 758 for his nephew Yan Jiming recalls deaths in his family during the An–Shi rebellion. Corrections and additions make the work a record of writing under the pressure of grief, as well as a text shaped by loyalty to the Tang. Another surviving letter, assigned by scholars to about 775, belongs to a less ceremonial world of communication. These works place an official’s handwriting between public responsibility and personal need. They also invite different kinds of reading: the dated mourning text anchors an event, while the letter’s date depends on historical comparison.
entrySummary.zh: 颜真卿的书法保存下来的，不只是受后世推崇的风格。758年为侄儿颜季明撰写的祭文，追忆安史战乱中的家族死亡。增补与涂改使它既是哀痛中写作的痕迹，也是带有忠于唐廷立场的文字。另一封传世信札，经学者据史事推定约作于775年，则属于较少礼仪色彩的通信世界。两类作品把官员的手迹置于公共责任与个人需要之间，也要求不同的阅读方式：祭文具有明确纪年，信札的年代则依赖历史比对。

reviewBasis.reviewMethod: Individually read assembled entry and cited source; portrait/date or surviving-document relationship stated explicitly

context.en: The entry uses Yan’s mourning text to approach the rebellion through family loss. This manuscript detail makes that named testimony visible.
context.zh: 本条通过颜氏祭文中的家族损失理解叛乱；手稿局部使这份具名见证可被直接观察。

entryTitle.en: An–Shi: a war that changed the Tang
entryTitle.zh: 安史之乱：改变唐朝的战争

entrySummary.en:
The uprising associated with An Lushan and Shi Siming brought war into the Tang heartland, including Chang'an and Luoyang. It disrupted families as well as imperial government. Du Fu's poems and Yan Zhenqing's mourning manuscript let us approach that upheaval through individual experiences.

The rebellion ended in 763, but the Tang survived until 907. The court faced powerful military governors and a changed relationship with neighbouring empires. Recovery did not restore the earlier balance of power; it also did not end Tang cultural life.
entrySummary.zh:
安禄山、史思明发动的叛乱将战争带进唐朝腹地，包括长安、洛阳。受到冲击的不仅是朝廷，还有无数家庭。杜甫的诗与颜真卿的祭文，使我们能从个人经历接近这场动荡。

叛乱在763年结束，唐朝却一直延续到907年。朝廷面对势力强大的节度使，与邻近帝国的关系也发生变化。战后恢复没有重建此前的权力格局，也没有使唐代文化生活就此终结。

entryTitle.en: Yan Zhenqing writes a requiem for his nephew
entryTitle.zh: 颜真卿书写《祭侄文稿》

entrySummary.en: After Yan Gaoqing and his son Jiming died resisting the An Lushan rebels, Yan Zhenqing sent his elder nephew Quanming to recover their remains. In 758 he wrote a requiem for Jiming. The surviving draft preserves crossed-out words and shifts from regular to running and cursive script, bringing a family’s wartime loss into the history of calligraphy.
entrySummary.zh: 颜杲卿与儿子季明在抵抗安史叛军时遇难后，颜真卿派长侄泉明前往收殓遗骸。758年，他为季明写下祭文。传世文稿保留涂改字句，楷、行、草笔法交织，使一个家族的战乱创痛留在了书法史中。

entryTitle.en: An encyclopedia that preserved parts of lost books
entryTitle.zh: 保存失传书籍片段的《永乐大典》

entrySummary.en:
A first compilation disappointed the Yongle emperor. The enlarged project brought scholars together in Nanjing to gather earlier writings into a manuscript reference work, completed in 1408. Readers found entries through a system based on sounds and rhymes.

Its survival tells another story. A later copy was made in 1562–1567, and most volumes eventually disappeared. Surviving portions preserve quotations from some books otherwise lost. An enormous collection could preserve knowledge while remaining difficult for most people to consult.
entrySummary.zh:
第一版汇编未令永乐帝满意，扩充后的工程将学者聚集在南京，收集前代著述，编成1408年完成的手写类书。读者通过音韵系统查找条目。

它的存世过程又是另一段故事：1562—1567年抄成的后世副本，其多数书册也逐渐散失。幸存部分保存了一些已经失传的书籍引文。庞大的收藏能够保存知识，同时又可能让大多数人难以查阅。

reviewBasis.reviewMethod: The exact assembled encyclopedia story names the Yongle emperor; the Palace Museum biography records the project beginning in Yongle 1. The portrait is patron identity, not a manuscript specimen.
